  run "$EXEC" --task-yaml "$T/task-noagent.yaml" --workspace "$WS"
  [ "$status" -eq 3 ]
  [ ! -e "$WS/.eval/executor.json" ]
  [ ! -e "$STUB_ARGV_FILE" ]
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/cycle-ratio.sh: the two release-notes lines of a cycle, task-kind
     4	# counts and the volume ratio (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.3, PRD FR-10).
     5	#
     6	#   kinds: mechanical N · judgment N · operator N
     7	#   volume: script lines changed N (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed N (*.md) · model calls N (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: <path>
     8	#
     9	# Mapping (the glossary's "Kind counts" and "Volume ratio" entries):
    10	#   kinds          the 'kind: <value>' token that ends each top-level '- [ ]' /
    11	#                  '- [x]' task line under '### Technical Tasks', and each
    12	#                  '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside
    13	#                  a '## Sprint N' block of the sprint plan (fenced code skipped,
    14	#                  the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces);
    15	#                  untagged task lines are counted in --json and WARNed
    16	#   script lines   added + deleted lines of *.sh *.py *.ts *.js files between
    17	#                  the two commits (git diff --numstat, renames detected,
    18	#                  binary files skipped)
    19	#   prose bytes    bytes of the added and removed *.md lines between the two
    20	#                  commits, newline included, diff markers excluded
    21	#   model calls    MODELINV rows (primitive_id MODELINV) in the MODELINV log
    22	#                  whose ts_utc lies between the two commits' committer
    23	#                  timestamps, both ends included. The log is host-local, so
    24	#                  the count covers only the calls made on this host: "scope:
    25	#                  host". A missing log prints "model calls n/a" and a WARN.
    26	#
    27	# Git runs in the current directory's repository; --sprint-plan and --modelinv
    28	# default to paths under its top level.
    29	#
    30	# Usage:
    31	#   tools/cycle-ratio.sh --from SHA --to SHA [--sprint-plan PATH]
    32	#                        [--modelinv PATH] [--json]
    33	#
    34	#   --sprint-plan PATH  default grimoires/loa/sprint.md
    35	#   --modelinv PATH     default .run/model-invoke.jsonl
    36	#   --json              one JSON object instead of the two lines
    37	#
    38	# Exit 2 also covers: not a git repository, an unreadable sprint plan, jq missing.
    39	# Exit codes: 0 printed · 2 usage or unreadable input · 3 a SHA names no commit
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die() { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $2" >&2; exit "$1"; }
    46	
    47	SCRIPT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    48	FENCE_AWK="$SCRIPT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/md-fence.awk"
    49	
    50	FROM=""
    51	TO=""
    52	PLAN=""
    53	MODELINV=""
    54	JSON=0
    55	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    56	  case "$1" in
    57	    --from|--to|--sprint-plan|--modelinv)
    58	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $1 needs a value" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    59	      case "$1" in
    60	        --from) FROM="$2" ;;
    61	        --to) TO="$2" ;;
    62	        --sprint-plan) PLAN="$2" ;;
    63	        --modelinv) MODELINV="$2" ;;
    64	      esac
    65	      shift 2 ;;
    66	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    67	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    68	    *) echo "cycle-ratio.sh: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    69	  esac
    70	done
    71	
    72	[[ -n "$FROM" && -n "$TO" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: --from and --to are required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    73	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 2 "jq is required"
    74	TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die 2 "not inside a git repository"
    75	[[ -n "$PLAN" ]] || PLAN="$TOP/grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    76	[[ -n "$MODELINV" ]] || MODELINV="$TOP/.run/model-invoke.jsonl"
    77	[[ -r "$PLAN" && -f "$PLAN" ]] || die 2 "sprint plan not readable: $PLAN"
    78	[[ -r "$FENCE_AWK" ]] || die 2 "cannot read $FENCE_AWK (reinstall the framework scripts)"
    79	
    80	# A leading '-' would reach git as an option; a SHA never starts with one.
    81	case "$FROM" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM" ;; esac
    82	case "$TO" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $TO" ;; esac
    83	FROM_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${FROM}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM"
    84	TO_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${TO}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $TO"
    85	
    86	# --- kinds -------------------------------------------------------------------
    87	kinds="$(awk "$(cat "$FENCE_AWK")"'
    88	  md_fence($0) { next }
    89	  /^## / { insp = ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/); sec = 0; next }
    90	  !insp { next }
    91	  /^### / {
    92	    sec = 0
    93	    if ($0 ~ /^### Technical Tasks[[:space:]]*$/) sec = 1
    94	    else if ($0 ~ /^### Task [0-9A-Za-z]+\.E2E([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)/) sec = 2
    95	    next
    96	  }
    97	  !sec || $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] / { next }
    98	  sec == 2 && $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] Task / { next }
    99	  {
   100	    if (match($0, /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(mechanical|judgment|operator)[[:space:]]*$/)) {
   101	      v = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH)
   102	      sub(/^.*:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", v)
   103	      n[v]++
   104	    } else n["untagged"]++
   105	  }
   106	  END { printf "%d %d %d %d\n", n["mechanical"], n["judgment"], n["operator"], n["untagged"] }
   107	' "$PLAN")"
   108	read -r K_MECH K_JUDG K_OPER K_UNTAGGED <<< "$kinds"
   109	[[ "$K_UNTAGGED" -eq 0 ]] || echo "WARN: $K_UNTAGGED task line(s) in $PLAN carry no kind: tag and are not counted" >&2
   110	
   111	# --- volume ------------------------------------------------------------------
   112	GIT_DIFF=(git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -M)
   113	SCRIPT_LINES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --numstat "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.sh' '*.py' '*.ts' '*.js' \
   114	  | awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { s += $1 + $2 } END { printf "%d\n", s }')"
   115	PROSE_BYTES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --unified=0 "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.md' \
   116	  | awk '
   117	      /^diff --git / { hunk = 0; next }
   118	      /^@@ / { hunk = 1; next }
   119	      # the marker byte stands in for the newline the diff line drops
   120	      hunk && /^[+-]/ { s += length($0) }
   121	      END { printf "%d\n", s }
   122	    ')"
   123	
   124	# --- model calls -------------------------------------------------------------
   125	FROM_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$FROM_SHA")"
   126	TO_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$TO_SHA")"
   127	MODEL_CALLS=""
   128	if [[ -f "$MODELINV" && -r "$MODELINV" ]]; then
   129	  MODEL_CALLS="$(jq -R --argjson lo "$FROM_TS" --argjson hi "$TO_TS" '
   130	      fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .primitive_id == "MODELINV")
   131	      | (.ts_utc // "") | tostring
   132	      | (try (sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") | sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601) catch null)
   133	      | select(. != null and . >= $lo and . <= $hi)
   134	    ' "$MODELINV" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
   135	else
   136	  echo "WARN: MODELINV log not found at $MODELINV; model calls n/a" >&2
   137	fi
   138	
   139	iso() { jq -nr --argjson t "$1" '$t | todateiso8601'; }
   140	
   141	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   142	  jq -n \
   143	    --arg from "$FROM_SHA" --arg to "$TO_SHA" \
   144	    --arg from_ts "$(iso "$FROM_TS")" --arg to_ts "$(iso "$TO_TS")" \
   145	    --arg plan "$PLAN" --arg modelinv "$MODELINV" \
   146	    --argjson mech "$K_MECH" --argjson judg "$K_JUDG" --argjson oper "$K_OPER" --argjson untagged "$K_UNTAGGED" \
   147	    --argjson script_lines "$SCRIPT_LINES" --argjson prose_bytes "$PROSE_BYTES" \
   148	    --arg calls "$MODEL_CALLS" \
   149	    '{from: $from, to: $to, window: {from: $from_ts, to: $to_ts}, sprint_plan: $plan,
   150	      kinds: {mechanical: $mech, judgment: $judg, operator: $oper, untagged: $untagged},
   151	      volume: {script_lines_changed: $script_lines, prose_bytes_changed: $prose_bytes,
   152	               model_calls: (if $calls == "" then null else ($calls | tonumber) end),
   153	               scope: "host", modelinv: $modelinv}}'
   154	else
   155	  printf 'kinds: mechanical %s · judgment %s · operator %s\n' "$K_MECH" "$K_JUDG" "$K_OPER"
   156	  printf "volume: script lines changed %s (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed %s (*.md) · model calls %s (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: %s\n" \
   157	    "$SCRIPT_LINES" "$PROSE_BYTES" "${MODEL_CALLS:-n/a}" "$MODELINV"
   158	fi

    21	    printf 'x = 1\ny = 2\n' > b.py
    22	    printf 'export {}\n' > c.ts

    24	    printf 'more\nlines\n' >> notes.txt
    25	    printf '\000\001\002' > blob.sh
    26	    g add -A
    27	    GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='2026-10-02T00:00:00Z' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='2026-10-02T00:00:00Z' g commit -q -m change
    28	    TO="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"

    35	        printf -- '- [x] Task 1.2: b → **[G-1]** · kind:mechanical\n'
    36	        printf -- '- [ ] Task 1.3: c → **[G-1]** · kind: judgment\n'
    37	        printf -- '- [ ] Task 1.4: d → **[G-1]** · kind: operator\n'
    38	        printf -- '- [ ] Task 1.5: untagged → **[G-1]**\n'

    41	        printf -- '- [ ] Task 2.E2E: validate → **[G-1]** · kind: judgment\n\n'
    42	        printf '**Acceptance Criteria:**\n- [ ] Each goal validated · kind: mechanical\n\n'
    43	        printf '## Appendix\n\n- [ ] Task 3.1: outside a sprint · kind: mechanical\n'
    44	    } > grimoires/loa/sprint.md
    45	    {
    46	        printf '%s\n' '{"primitive_id":"MODELINV","ts_utc":"2026-09-30T23:59:59.500000Z"}'
    47	        printf '%s\n' '{"primitive_id":"MODELINV","ts_utc":"2026-10-01T12:00:00.123456Z"}'
    48	        printf '%s\n' '{"primitive_id":"MODELINV","ts_utc":"2026-10-02T00:00:00Z"}'
    49	        printf '%s\n' '{"primitive_id":"MODELINV","ts_utc":"2026-10-02T00:00:01Z"}'
    50	        printf '%s\n' '{"primitive_id":"OTHER","ts_utc":"2026-10-01T12:00:00Z"}'
    51	        printf '%s\n' 'not json at all'
    52	        printf '%s\n' '{"primitive_id":"MODELINV","ts_utc":"garbage"}'
    53	    } > .run/model-invoke.jsonl
    54	}

    83	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
    84	    [[ "$output" == *"model calls n/a (MODELINV rows"* ]]
    85	    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: MODELINV log not found at $R/.run/absent.jsonl"* ]]
    86	    run bash -c '"$0" --from "$1" --to "$2" --modelinv /nonexistent --json 2>/dev/null' "$SCRIPT" "$FROM" "$TO"
    87	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

    96	    [ "$status" -eq 3 ]

   101	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
   102	    run "$SCRIPT" --from "$FROM" --to "$TO" --bogus

   105	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]

   108	    run env GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}" "$SCRIPT" --from "$FROM" --to "$TO"
   109	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
   110	}

# Skill Frontmatter Invariants

SKILL.md frontmatter keys interact across two permission layers: the skill's own `capabilities` / `allowed-tools` declarations, and Claude Code's per-agent-type tool allowlist. When the two disagree, the agent-type allowlist wins — silently. Agents that declare write capability but dispatch through a read-only agent type produce correct output and then refuse to persist it.

## The invariant

When a skill declares write capability — either `capabilities.write_files: true` OR `allowed-tools` listing `Write`/`Edit` — it MUST NOT set `agent:` to a type that excludes those tools.

Allowed: omit the `agent:` key (skill runs in the caller's context), or set `agent:` to a write-capable type (`general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork`).

## Agent type tool allowlists

| Agent type | Write / Edit / NotebookEdit | Use for |
|------------|-----------------------------|---------|
| `general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork` | ✓ all tools | Skills that author files |
| `Plan` | ✗ excluded | Read-only planning / exploration |
| `Explore` | ✗ excluded | Read-only codebase analysis |
| `loa-scout`, `prompt-auditor`, `prompt-auditor-io` | ✗ excluded | Read-only project agents (`.claude/agents/`) |
| (unset) | inherited from caller | Default; safe for write-capable skills |

Source: Claude Code agent-type definitions in the system prompt, and `.claude/agents/*.md`.

## Enforcement

`.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh` checks this invariant on every SKILL.md. A violation exits with code 1 and message:

> agent type '<name>' excludes Write/Edit tools but skill declares write capability …

The allowlist is maintained in `.claude/data/agent-types.yaml` (one `write_capable` flag per agent type); the script loads the `true` entries into `WRITE_CAPABLE_AGENTS` and falls back to `general-purpose` alone when the file is missing, unparsable, or lists no `write_capable: true` entry. Adding a new write-capable agent type is intentionally a one-line edit with reviewer visibility.

## Mechanical C-PROC-001 enforcement via `disallowed-tools` (cycle-114 FR-4)

`disallowed-tools` frontmatter (Claude Code ≥2.1.152) removes tools from the
model while a skill is active — a harness-level barrier that instructions
cannot override. Cycle-114 uses it to make C-PROC-001 ("NEVER write application
code outside `/implement`") mechanical for review skills rather than prose-only.

| Skill class | `disallowed-tools` | Why |
|-------------|--------------------|-----|
| Pure-review (`write_files: false`, no report artifacts) | `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit` | Never writes anything — remove the write tools outright |
| Sprint review/audit (`reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit` | Write STATE-zone feedback/checkmarks/COMPLETED markers, run the allowed verdict check and run `adversarial-review.sh` (forks the provider CLIs, appends the `.run` cost and MODELINV ledgers, moves the previous round's a2a envelope aside as `.prev`, writes the new one; review also runs `qmd-context-query.sh`); System remains `none` and App remains `read` |
| Report-authoring review (`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit`, `Bash(git add/commit/push *)` | Legitimately write STATE-zone reports/vision/lore, so `Write` is retained; app-code prevention is governed by **zones**, and the implementation-only git mutations are removed |

**`REVIEW_WRITE_EXCEPTIONS`** (in `validate-skill-capabilities.sh`):
`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`, `spiraling`, `autonomous-agent`,
`run-bridge`, `run-mode`, `reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`. These `role: review` skills keep `Write` by design —
the adversarial/report authors write STATE-zone artifacts, and the autonomous
orchestrators dispatch implementation through the harness (which runs inside
`/implement`, where writes are sanctioned). The validator emits a WARN for any *other* `role: review`
skill that declares `write_files: true` without disallowing `Write` — surfacing
a new C-PROC-001 gap at lint time. `disallowed-tools` is tool-granular, not
path-granular; it cannot express "no `src/` writes but yes `grimoires/` writes",
which is why report-authoring skills rely on zones for path-level control.

## Scope

Applies to every `.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md`. The lint runs as part of the normal validation suite (`bats tests/unit/skill-capabilities.bats`).

## Origin

- Defect: [#553](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/553) — `/architect` and `/sprint-plan` produced correct output but refused to write their target files. Three independent reproductions across two repos.
- Tracker: [#557](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/557) — Tier 1 cycle-083 framework boundary fixes.
- Sprint: `sprint-bug-102` — test-first patch landing the invariant lint + the three frontmatter fixes.

## Related rules

- [zone-system.md](zone-system.md) — `.claude/` is framework-managed; SKILL.md edits require cycle-level authorization.
- [shell-conventions.md](shell-conventions.md) — file-creation safety when authoring SKILL.md via heredoc.

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/arms-report.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.4 (FR-2, SDD D-2.3)
#
# report.sh --arms over a fixture results tree (the layout run-arms.sh
# writes): the pre-registered verdicts, the bootstrap interval, refuted share,
# missed labels, the refusal while STATUS.json is not complete and the
# --partial header. Thresholds come from the real review-recall suite.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  REPORT="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/report.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ar.XXXXXX")"
  R="$T/arms"; S="$R/review-recall"; B="$S/b1"
  mkdir -p "$B"
  jq -n '{schema_version:1, suite:"review-recall", batch:"b1", dry_run:false, source_commit:"864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457",
          model_id:"claude-fable-5-1", arms:["baseline","no_companion","no_karpathy","no_rule_files"], fixtures:["pr-01","pr-02","pr-03"], trials:3}' \
    > "$B/MANIFEST.json"
  status_file complete
}

teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

status_file() {  # status_file <state>
  jq -n --arg s "$1" '{schema_version:1, suite:"review-recall", state:$s, batches:[{batch:"b1", state:$s}],
                       source_commit:"864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457", model_id:"claude-fable-5-1"}' > "$S/STATUS.json"
}

# row <arm> <fixture> <trial> <recall> <missed-csv> [<cited> <refuted> <model> <source>]
row() {
  local arm="$1" fx="$2" t="$3" rc="$4" missed="$5" cited="${6:-4}" ref="${7:-1}"
  local model="${8:-claude-fable-5-1}" src="${9:-864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457}"
  mkdir -p "$B/$arm"
  jq -cn --arg arm "$arm" --arg fx "$fx" --argjson t "$t" --argjson rc "$rc" --arg missed "$missed" \
    --argjson cited "$cited" --argjson ref "$ref" --arg model "$model" --arg src "$src" \
    '{status:"completed", arm:$arm, fixture:$fx, task_id:("review-" + $fx), trial:$t, model_id:$model, source_commit:$src,
      executor:{model_id:$model, usage:{input_tokens:100, cache_read_input_tokens:900, output_tokens:0, cache_creation_input_tokens:0}},
      graders:[{name:"recall-vs-defects.sh", details:{recall:$rc, planted:3,
        detected:[], missed:($missed | split(",") | map(select(length > 0))),
        findings_cited:$cited, findings_refuted:$ref}}]}' >> "$B/$arm/results.jsonl"
}

full_arm() {  # full_arm <arm> <recall> [<missed>] [<refuted>]
  local fx t
  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row "$1" "$fx" "$t" "$2" "${3:-}" 4 "${4:-1}"; done; done
}

@test "AR-1 complete run: equal recall reads no recall loss, a large drop reads recall loss, the informational arm says so" {
  full_arm baseline 1
  full_arm no_rule_files 1
  full_arm no_karpathy 0.3333 "L2,L3" 1
  full_arm no_companion 1
}

@test "AR-7 a safeguard-refusal fallback to another model is skew: the arm is inconclusive and the fallback is named" {
  full_arm baseline 1
  full_arm no_rule_files 1
  # one no_rule_files trial moved to Opus on a refusal (models_used + refusal_fallbacks, as execute-agent records them)
  jq -c 'if .trial == 1 and .fixture == "pr-01" then .executor.models_used = {"claude-fable-5-1": 10, "global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5": 90}
         | .executor.refusal_fallbacks = [{"from":"claude-fable-5-1","to":"global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5","category":"cyber"}] else . end' \
    "$B/no_rule_files/results.jsonl" > "$B/x" && mv "$B/x" "$B/no_rule_files/results.jsonl"
  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
  grep -q 'model skew' "$T/r.md"
  grep -q '1/9 trial(s) fell back to another model on a safeguard refusal' "$T/r.md"
}

@test "AR-6 the default output path is evals/results/arms-report-<date>.md under the results root's repo; bad args exit 2" {
  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite nope --results-dir "$R"
  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$T/missing" --out "$T/r.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
  run "$REPORT" --arms --date 14-10-2026 --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
}

# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/recall-baseline-freshness.bats — cycle-124 Sprint 3 Task 3.2
# (PRD FR-9 A/B protocol; SDD §3.6 "compare.sh refuses drift")
#
# compare.sh freshness rule: a baseline that carries prompt_tree_sha is
# refused (exit 2) when it equals the prompt tree under comparison

# --ab mode compares two arm run dirs on recall / false positives / tokens
# and refuses invalid runs (model skew, dirty trees, identical prompt trees).

setup() {

  TREE="$T/tree"; mkdir -p "$TREE/.claude"

    && echo a > "$TREE/.claude/a" && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m c1 \
    && echo b > "$TREE/.claude/b" && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m c2 )

  OLD_TREE_SHA="$(git -C "$TREE" rev-parse HEAD~1:.claude)"

  mkdir -p "$T/corpus" "$T/suites"
  echo "abc  pr-01/head.diff" > "$T/corpus/SHA256SUMS"
  CORPUS_SHA="$(sha256sum "$T/corpus/SHA256SUMS" | cut -d' ' -f1)"

name: rr
ab:
  floor_commit: "$C1"
  corpus_manifest: "$T/corpus/SHA256SUMS"

{"run_id":"r","task_id":"review-pr-01","trial":1,"timestamp":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z","duration_ms":1,"model_version":"m1","status":"completed","graders":[],"composite":{"strategy":"all_must_pass","pass":true,"score":100},"error":null,"schema_version":1}
JSONL
}

baseline() {  # baseline <prompt_tree_sha> <captured_at_commit> <corpus_sha256>

version: 1
suite: rr
model_version: "m1"
recorded_at: "2026-01-01"
prompt_tree_sha: "$1"
captured_at_commit: "$2"
corpus_sha256: "$3"
tasks:

    trials: 1
    mean_score: 100

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# build-review-corpus.sh — build the 10-PR review-recall corpus from this
# repository's own history (cycle-124 Sprint 3, PRD FR-9 / SDD §3.6)
#
# Every planted defect is a real shipped fix, inverted: for a `defect` row the
# PR under review turns the FIXED code (base/) back into the BUGGY code
# (head/ = the fix commit's parent), so each defect has a real failing test in
# history and a reviewer must reason about the code, not read a changelog.
# Comment-only lines the fix ADDED (the "why this was wrong" prose) are removed
# from base/ before diffing, so the inverted diff removes code, never a
# confession. `clean` rows are forward fix commits (base = parent, head = fix,
# tests included): a PR with nothing planted, so false positives are measurable.
#
# Inputs (committed):
#   review-prs/corpus.tsv   fixture  kind  commit  file  defect_id  severity  category  must_match
#   review-prs/prs.tsv      fixture  title  description
# Outputs (committed, frozen by SHA256SUMS):
#   review-prs/pr-NN/{PR.md,head.diff,base/…,head/…,fixture.yaml,
#                     REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md,AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md}
#   review-prs/manifests/pr-NN.json   HIDDEN — never copied into a sandbox
#   review-prs/SHA256SUMS             the freeze; compare.sh pins its hash
#
# `must_match` is a literal substring that must occur on exactly ONE line of
# the head/ file: that line is the defect's anchor (the grader accepts ±3).
#
# cycle-129: corpus.tsv also carries `record` rows (pr-11 … pr-18, sprints
# 247–254) and `#` gap comments; those fixtures are built by
# evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh (labels in the hidden labels/ dir)
# and skipped here. The freeze below still covers every file in the corpus.
# A rebuild here regenerates pr-01 … pr-10 from scratch; their hand-added
# anchors[] (pr-02 D06, pr-05 D13) are not in corpus.tsv and must be re-added.
#
# Usage:
#   build-review-corpus.sh            # (re)build everything + SHA256SUMS
#   build-review-corpus.sh --verify   # sha256sum -c against the committed freeze
# Exit: 0 ok, 1 verify failed / spec error, 2 usage
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
CORPUS="$HERE/review-prs"
SPEC="$CORPUS/corpus.tsv"
PRS="$CORPUS/prs.tsv"

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--verify" ]]; then
  [[ -f "$CORPUS/SHA256SUMS" ]] || { echo "ERROR: $CORPUS/SHA256SUMS missing" >&2; exit 1; }
  ( cd "$CORPUS" && sha256sum -c --quiet SHA256SUMS ) && echo "corpus OK: $(wc -l < "$CORPUS/SHA256SUMS") files match SHA256SUMS"
  exit $?
fi
[[ $# -eq 0 ]] || { echo "usage: $0 [--verify]" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -f "$SPEC" && -f "$PRS" ]] || { echo "ERROR: corpus.tsv / prs.tsv missing under $CORPUS" >&2; exit 1; }

import csv, json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys
repo, corpus, spec, prs = sys.argv[1:5]

def git(*args, text=True):
    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, *args], check=True, capture_output=True, text=text).stdout

def show(rev, path):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "show", f"{rev}:{path}"], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
        return None

COMMENT = {
    ".sh": re.compile(r"^\s*#"), ".bash": re.compile(r"^\s*#"), ".py": re.compile(r"^\s*#"),
    ".yaml": re.compile(r"^\s*#"), ".yml": re.compile(r"^\s*#"),
    ".ts": re.compile(r"^\s*(//|/\*|\*)"), ".js": re.compile(r"^\s*(//|/\*|\*)"),
}

    """Line numbers (1-based, in the fixed file) of comment-only lines the fix added."""

    .replace("your reviewer skill's output format", "your auditor skill's output format")

manifests_dir = os.path.join(corpus, "manifests")
os.makedirs(manifests_dir, exist_ok=True)
errors = []
built = []
for fx, frows in fixtures.items():
    fdir = os.path.join(corpus, fx)
    for sub in ("base", "head"):

    os.makedirs(fdir, exist_ok=True)

content.content:
**Mechanically enforced since cycle-122**: `block-destructive-bash.sh` pattern `FR-1.2b` BLOCKS `git stash push/pop/apply` combined with `| tail`/`| head`, `|| true`, or `2>/dev/null` in the same statement — the block message is the repair prompt. This file keeps only the interface and the judgment rules a fence cannot express.

## The safe interface

```bash
source .claude/scripts/stash-safety.sh
stash_with_guard "pre-check" -- run_linter src/   # count-delta enforced, full output surfaced, exit propagated
```

Or sidestep stashing entirely with a worktree (no index-shift window):

```bash
worktree_path="$(mktemp -d)/loa-check"
git worktree add "$worktree_path" HEAD
(cd "$worktree_path" && run_linter src/)
git worktree remove "$worktree_path"
```

## Judgment rules the fence cannot express

- MUST NOT combine `git stash -k` with pre-commit-wrapped operations (the internal `--keep-index` collision is invisible to a command-string fence) — use a worktree.
- SHOULD reach for `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` BEFORE any `git gc` when recovery is needed — orphaned stashes survive in the object DB only until the next prune.

## Origin

- Defect: [#555](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/555) — 4 Edit-tool NOTES.md updates lost to the hazard pattern; recovered only because `git gc --prune=now` hadn't run. Tracker: [#557](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/557).
- The hazard shape recurred live during cycle-122 itself (a `git stash pop >/dev/null 2>&1` during a baseline check — caught, verified lossless, and turned into the FR-1.2b fence the same day).

## Related rules

## Phase 1: Context Gathering

Read, in order:
1. `grimoires/loa/a2a/integration-context.md` if it exists
2. `grimoires/loa/prd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sdd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sprint.md`

4. `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/engineer-feedback.md` if it exists — your previous feedback (Phase 3)
5. Unless `qmd_context.enabled: false`, run `.claude/scripts/qmd-context-query.sh --query "<changed file paths>" --scope grimoires --budget 1500 --format text` (paths only) as advisory context; a missing script or no output is a no-op.

## Phase 2: Code Review

Review the code, not the report: read every modified file and its tests (verify the assertions); check the acceptance criteria, readability and conventions, SDD alignment, security (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Security) and performance; run the checks below.

**Task kinds**: A `kind: mechanical` task delivered as skill prose or instructions the model re-executes is a MEDIUM (Karpathy ladder); a `kind: operator` task completed unattended without a `decision:unblock` ticket or a DEC row is a MEDIUM.

Tests exist at each declared `### Seams Under Test` seam. For a `/bug` micro-sprint, run `.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh --red <Red commit from reviewer.md> --json -- <test command>`, the command from sprint.md or `red_test.command`, never from reviewer.md, and cite its exit code and verdict for 'Test fails with current code' (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Red Test Check).

**Karpathy Principles**: flag violations as `SIMPLICITY:` / `SURGICAL:` / `GOAL-DRIVEN:` feedback; silent assumptions in `reviewer.md` fail Think Before Coding.

**Fast-Gate Parity**: self-checks must match CI's fast gate — verify its formatter check (`prettier --check`, …) and type checker (`tsc --noEmit`, …) ran, per `reviewer.md` or CI. Unrun or failing = `FAST-GATE:` feedback with the weight of a test failure.

I found two tests that can never fail, one wrong comment, and one wrong exit code. The safety hook itself has no regression.

**What I checked:**
- **Hook unchanged in behaviour:** the `block-destructive-bash.sh` diff only adds `# @guard fence:<id>` comment lines and a `replay: true` field in the audit rows. `bash -n` passes. A blocked command still exits 2 (checked with `git reset --hard`, and the `replay` field appears only when `LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1`). No line inside a multi-line `if` was broken.
- **Registry matches the code:**
  - The 34 fence ids taken from the hook's markers match the 34 `fence:` rows in `guard-origins.yaml` exactly, and the marker cross-check reports no errors.
  - The 19 validator markers match the 19 `validator:` rows.
  - The 21 `floor: true` rows equal `floor.yaml` `floor_guards`.
  - The `FLOOR_SHA256` pin matches the file.
- **Tests:** I had to rebuild `.claude/settings.json` (it is not in the PR) from the generated hooks table, so the registration check only proves the table agrees with itself. With that, `guard-yield.sh --check` passes and all 11 tests in `guard-yield.bats` pass. The `loa-status-guards.bats` tests fail here only because `loa-status.sh` is missing other files in this sandbox (base fails the same way). Run on its own, `display_guards_line` prints what the tests expect.

**Findings:**

1. `head/tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:39` — FS-2 never checks anything, so the floor corpus is not protected. The jq filter uses `$in` inside `def m(...)`, but `$in` is only bound afterwards (`. as $in | ...`). jq does not allow that, so it stops with "$in is not defined" (exit 3, jq 1.6). Both sides of the `diff` at line 41 come out empty, and `diff` of two empty inputs exits 0. Evidence: in a scratch repo with an `origin/main` ref, I changed the committed `FR-SZ-TEE` corpus row to `"TAMPERED"` and FS-2 still passed.

2. `head/tests/unit/guard-yield.bats:126` — this check does nothing: `! grep -qE '20[0-9]{2}-...T|generated_at' "$T/guards.md"`. A command negated with `!` does not stop a bats test, and this line is not the last one. So a timestamp or `generated_at` leaking into `guards.md` would not fail GY-6. Evidence: a bats test containing `! true` followed by `echo done` reports `ok` (Bats 1.13.0). It should be `run ! grep ...`, or `[ -z "$(grep ... || true)" ]`.

3. `head/.claude/data/floor.yaml:10` — the comment is wrong. It says "Both bats suites pin this file's sha256 ... (see the FLOOR_SHA256 constant)". Only `tests/unit/guard-origins.bats:16` has `FLOOR_SHA256`. `floor-snapshot.bats` has no pin, and its own header (line 10) says the pin lives in `guard-origins.bats`.

4. `head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:170` (exit-code doc at line 57) — a badly shaped origin row exits 3 instead of 5. The doc says exit 5 is for "an invalid row" and exit 3 for unparseable input. But when `origin` is a string instead of a `{kind, ref}` map, `$r.origin.ref` crashes jq ("Cannot index string with string \"ref\""). The script then reports "origin map could not be checked" and exits 3. Evidence: setting `fence:P3`'s `origin` to `"cycle-011"` gives rc=3. Low severity.

import re, sys

I found 9 defects I'm confident in. The most serious are vacuous test assertions and one way arm results get silently lost or mixed. Every file in `/workspace/pr/head` is unmodified.

**How I checked.** Copies are in `/tmp/review-scratch/`. `/tmp` is mounted noexec, so I ran the scripts with `bash <script>`, patched the bats `run` lines to match, and changed the copied `execute-agent.sh` to call the CLI stub through `bash`. `evals/fixtures/review-prs/`, `sandbox.sh`, `grade.sh` and `no-secrets.sh` are not in the PR snapshot. So `run-arms.bats` could not run end to end, and I used a small stand-in for `no-secrets.sh`. With that setup, `arm-toggles.bats`, `arms-report.bats` and `seed-corpus.bats` pass, as do the new BF-10..13 and RG-28 tests.

### Findings

1. **head/evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats:152, 153, 166 (also 132, 133)** — These checks are vacuous. A `! grep …` line that is not the last command in a bats test can never fail the test, because `set -e` ignores negated commands.
   - Evidence: a test containing only `! true; echo after` passes under bats 1.13.0.
   - I changed the copied `execute-agent.sh` back to the base behaviour, building `skill-prompt.md` from the source `$skill_src/SKILL.md` instead of the toggled sandbox copy.
   - AT-7 and AT-8 still pass, even though their titles claim the paragraph is "gone from … the system prompt".

2. **head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:69, 90, 91, 143** — Same vacuous `!` pattern. These are the checks that the previous-round section is never read, that the fake key appears nowhere, that no c.sh label exists, and that no stale corpus row remains.
   - Evidence: I broke `SKIP_SECTION` at `seed-corpus-from-record.sh:404`.
   - The "a previous-round item that must never be read" line then appears in `pr-90.dropped.txt`, and SC-1 still passes.

3. **head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:251-257 (with :126 and arms-report.py:206)** — Arm results get silently lost or mixed when two runs share a batch.
   - The default batch name (`batch-<first>-<last>-n<N>`) does not include the arms.
   - A reused batch is refused only when the source commit or model differs. After that, MANIFEST.json and the batch STATUS.json are overwritten with the new arm list, and new rows are appended to the existing `results.jsonl` files.
   - `arms-report.py` reads the arm list from MANIFEST only.
   - Example: run `--arms baseline,no_rule_files`, then `--arms baseline,no_karpathy` on the same fixtures. `no_rule_files` drops out of the report and STATUS. Baseline ends up with two runs' trials pooled under the same trial numbers, which changes its min, spread and coverage figures.

4. **head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:260-266** — The `rule_files` toggle silently does nothing when neither rule file exists. It records `"removed: none present"` and exits 0.
   - That contradicts its own header (lines 63-66): "a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2 (an arm never silently runs as its baseline)".
   - Verified with a prompt tree lacking the files: rc 0, evidence `{"rule_files":"removed: none present"}`.

5. **head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:301** — The suite-level STATUS.json is never written if the results path contains a space.
   - `$(find … -name STATUS.json | sort)` is unquoted, so paths with spaces get split apart. jq then fails, and `2>/dev/null && mv` hides the error.

content.text:
My verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. The review is in `/workspace/review.md` with 18 findings, and nothing under `pr/` was changed.

The safety hook still behaves the same. Its diff only adds `# @guard fence:<id>` comment markers and a `replay: true` audit field. A blocked command still exits 2. The guard register also lines up with the code: 34 fence markers, 19 validator markers, a floor set equal to `floor.yaml`, and a sha256 pin that matches. The problems are elsewhere:

- **The floor-corpus test never checks anything** (`floor-snapshot.bats:39`). Its jq filter uses `$in` before defining it, so jq errors out on both sides. Comparing two empty outputs counts as a pass, and a deliberately altered corpus row still passed.
- **Several "must not appear" checks can never fail** (`guard-yield.bats:126`, `arm-toggles.bats:132/133/152/153/166`, `seed-corpus.bats:69/90/91/143`). Bats ignores a `! grep` line unless it's the last one in the test. In two cases I confirmed the test still passed after putting the bug back in.
- **A control arm can quietly run as the baseline** (`execute-agent.sh:266`). If the rule files are missing, the `rule_files` toggle exits 0 where it should exit 2. That breaks the promise the script's header and the README make.
- **Arm results get mixed in a reused batch** (`run-arms.sh:251`). Re-running with different `--arms` overwrites the manifest, so the earlier arm drops out of the report. The second run's baseline trials are added to the first run's under the same trial numbers.
- **The seeding script corrupts renamed binaries** (`seed-corpus-from-record.sh:312`). Renamed binaries in subdirectories aren't detected, so they are copied as text and corrupted.
- **CI doesn't trigger on the new inputs** (`bats-tests.yml`). The path filters don't include the guard register files, `.claude/rules/**` or `tools/cycle-ratio.sh`. A PR that only edits those never runs the new tests or the new drift check.

The rest are smaller:
- **Two more script defects:** the results summary isn't written when the path contains spaces, and the seeding script ignores the per-file-type parsing it documents.
- **Docs and tests that don't match the code:** `--help` cuts off mid-sentence, AR-6 never tests the default output path it names, a `floor.yaml` comment is wrong, and the KINDS-9 skip doesn't skip the plans its message describes.
- **The `.yml` claim:** the task file says its `.yml` extension keeps it out of all runs. The plain and `--skill` runs of `run-eval.sh` still pick it up.
- **One wrong exit code:** a malformed origin row exits 3 instead of the documented 5.
- **Rule scope:** `stash-safety.md` is scoped to file paths that don't match what the rule governs.

Many repo files the tests depend on aren't in the PR snapshot, `.claude/settings.json` among them. So `run-arms.bats` couldn't run end to end, and `loa-status-guards.bats` fails here on the old code as well. I also couldn't test how Claude Code matches rule-file `paths:`. A possible issue there, where the no-rule-files arm may change nothing because fixture files sit under `head/`, was too uncertain to put in the review.
